title: One source's extract
description: workareas/<workarea>/distil/extract/<source slug>.json: what one source says, one claim per observable fact, with provenance, before any reconciling. A source is extracted in parts: the characterise agent cuts it into the parts partition.schema.json defines, one extract agent per part writes distil/extract/<source slug>.part<N>.json in this same shape (its `structure` says what the part covered, and it has no `scopeHash`), and `tim distil merge-extract` joins the parts into this one file, in part order, and stamps its scope hash. `tim distil check --stage extract` validates the file and every part against this schema, and also checks what a schema cannot: `source` names this file's source, `scopeHash` matches the source's kind, locator and scope today, claim ids are unique across every extract in the workarea, no claim id ends in -m<N> (that suffix is kept for claims a verifier finds missing), each part's claims use its prefix or an id it keeps, and the file is exactly its parts merged.

source.description: The source id from sources.json, such as "confluence:6518997274".

structure.description: What the source is and how it is laid out, written before any claim: characterise first, extract second. In the merged extract, the partition's structure followed by each part's own. In a part file, what the part read and what it covered.

scopeHash.description: The source's scope hash when it was extracted, as `tim distil status` reports it: the sha256, in hex, of its kind, locator and scope. `tim distil stamp` writes it. A different hash today means the source's scope changed, so the extract is stale. An extract with no hash (one written before the hash existed) is stale too, until `tim distil stamp` adopts it or the source is extracted again.

claims.description: Every claim, in the order the source makes them.

text.description: Text that is not empty or only whitespace.

claim.description: One observable fact the source states: something a user, operator or other system can observe, never a file, class or function. It records what the source says, without reconciling it with other sources.

id.description: A short prefix for the source and a number, such as "conf-001" or "tests-014". Unique across the whole workarea, because requirements cite claims by id alone.

statement.description: The fact, in plain English. For an inferred claim, it says why it follows.

kind.description: What sort of fact it is. A gap is a confidence, never a kind.

ref.description: Where in the source: a section, heading, table row, page file, or file and line for a repo.

quote.description: The source's own words, verbatim. Only a gap, where the source says nothing, may leave it empty.

confidence.description: verbatim: the source says it. inferred: read between the lines, and the statement says why. gap: the source should say something here and does not.

note.description: Anything else the extractor wants the verifier or reconciler to know about this claim.

then.description: A verbatim or inferred claim quotes the words it rests on.
